name: Metadata for publication "The General Movement Optimality Score-Revised (GMOS-R) with Socioeconomically Stratified Percentile Ranks"
description: This paper is based on general movement optimality score - revised (GMOS-R) ratings of non public infant video recordings. We applied the GMOS-R to an international sample of 1983 infants (32% female, 44% male, and 24% not disclosed), assessed in the extremely and very preterm period (10%), moderate (12%) and late (22%) preterm periods, at term (25%), and post-term age (31%).
